items.source_en:
The body is still, their suit perforated by ballistic impacts. The self sealing fabric tried to compensate, but against this many shots, it never stood a chance. The scientists helmet display flickers weakly, warning of critical system failure.

A datapad is clutched in one hand, the cracked screen still displaying a series of incomplete readings. A final log entry is partially typed, trailing off midsentence:

They saw me. No time to...

A Mercenary insignia is scrawled across the suit in deep knife gouges, a crude signature of those who kill without reason. The weapon fire was precise, deliberate. Whatever the scientist was studying, someone did not want them to finish.
items.legacy_ko:
시신은 고요하며 우주복은 탄환 충격으로 구멍이 뚫려 있다. 자가 밀봉 직물이 보상하려 했으나, 이 정도의 사격 앞에서는 속수무책이었다. 과학자의 헬멧 디스플레이는 희미하게 깜빡이며 치명적인 시스템 오류를 경고한다.

한 손에는 데이터패드가 쥐어져 있고, 깨진 화면에는 일련의 불완전한 판독값이 표시되어 있다. 마지막 로그 항목은 문장 중간에 끊긴 채 입력되어 있다:

놈들이 날 봤어. 시간이 없...

우주복 도금에는 이유 없이 살인을 저지르는 자들의 거친 서명인 용병 휘장이 깊은 칼자국으로 새겨져 있다. 무기 사격은 정밀하고 의도적이었다. 과학자가 무엇을 연구했든, 누군가는 그들이 끝내기를 원치 않았다.

items.source_en:
When I heard the learned star-watcher,

When the starcharts and telemetry were arranged in holos before me,

When I was shown the equations and drift calculations, to map, measure, and predict,

When I sat and listened as the scholar spoke, the council enraptured,

How soon I felt restless and unwell,

Till rising and drifting out, I wandered alone,

Into the silent void beyond the durasteel walls, and from time to time,

Looked up in wonder at the stars.

[An excerpt from the lost works of Zol Variss, an Outer Rim poet who believed the stars should be felt, not studied.]

locations.vanilla_source_en:
When I heard the learn'd astronomer, 

When the proofs, the figures, were ranged in columns before me, 

When I was shown the charts and diagrams, to add, divide, and measure them, 

When I sitting heard the astronomer where he lectured with much applause in the lecture-room, 

How soon unaccountable I became tired and sick, 

Till rising and gliding out I wander'd off by myself, 

In the mystical moist night-air, and from time to time, 

Look'd up in perfect silence at the stars. 

[Walt Whitman's When I Heard the Learn'd Astronomer, while only one stanza, neatly encapsulates the author's disdain for the scientific overanalysis of nature's beauty.]

locations.vanilla_source_en:
Doriane,

You must've thought I was crazy, but now you see, right? Of all the people I could've chosen - I know you will fill the role of Mantis the best.

In these computers you will find the history of the Mantis. What the Mantis is today, it wasn't always the case. When reading the logs about the first Mantis - don't judge her too harshly. It was a volatile time and before she passed the mantle she recognized that the Mantis could be more than an opportunity to make money. It could be a symbol.

Make the Settled Systems safer. Strike fear into the heart of those that believe they are above the law, above reproach. But most importantly - keep the secrets safe.

Now I'm off to retirement. Don't try to contact me, you won't be able to find me. I've left all you need here.

-The Former Mantis
